intent: Lay out one message of a conversation as a row, placing an avatar beside a column that holds the message's header, visible surface and footer, on the side the message belongs to.
typical_uses: One message in a conversation thread, from either side, with or without an avatar
A message that carries a sender name above it or a status line or actions below it

dont_use_when.situation: The visible surface of the message itself, its fill, frame and text
A one-line status or event in the conversation with no avatar, header or footer
The scrolling frame around a whole transcript

invariants.text: `align` is written to the row as `data-align` and is the only alignment input of the family; no part takes an `align` of its own, each reacts to the row's attribute through message.module.css. A Bubble inside the row takes its own `align`, which the row does not set; the Bubble's notched speaker-side corner follows the Bubble's own `align`, so an end-side row needs `align="end"` on its Bubble as well.

With `align="end"` the row lays its children out in reverse (`flex-direction: row-reverse`), so a MessageAvatar written first sits after MessageContent on the inline axis, and every direct child of a MessageContent inside the row aligns to the end edge.
Message and every part render a plain div with no role, no aria attribute and no live region of their own; a message appearing announces nothing to assistive tech.

good.title: A message from the other side with an avatar, a sender name and a status line
The current user's own message on the end side
good.code:
<Message align="end">
  <MessageContent>
    <Bubble variant="secondary" align="end">
      <BubbleContent>What did the last deploy change?</BubbleContent>
    </Bubble>
  </MessageContent>
</Message>

bad.title: The sender name written as a direct child of the row
bad.why: Message is a flex row, so the header is laid out to the side of the content column rather than above the bubble; inside MessageContent it stacks above the surface.
